_comment_purpose: redroid-seccomp-l0b.json — PROPOSED hardened seccomp BPF profile for a Magisk-rooted ReDroid 12 L0b cell. This is a PROPOSAL ARTIFACT (Phase 6), NOT the pinned production profile. It re-permits the 4 load-bearing syscalls (personality, arch_prctl, mount, setns) that Phase 5 proved are required for a Magisk-rooted ReDroid 12 to boot under enforcing seccomp. UPDATE 2026-06-01 (seccomp-promotion-audit §5 recommendations APPLIED + empirically re-tested, see proof/seccomp-promotion-audit/APPLIED.md): the formerly-unconditional 4-name ALLOW has been SPLIT — arch_prctl + mount remain unfiltered (TLS / fstype-is-a-pointer, both non-narrowable), while personality is now arg-filtered to persona∈{0 (PER_LINUX), 0xffffffff (query)} (blocks ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE/READ_IMPLIES_EXEC) and setns is now arg-filtered to nstype==CLONE_NEWNS (blocks PID/NET/USER/cgroup-ns entry and the nstype==0 any-type escape form). Both arg-filters were boot+root re-tested (boot_completed=1, su uid=0, magisk 30600) and the setns filter was strace-proven not to EPERM magiskd. defaultAction remains SCMP_ACT_ERRNO (still enforcing, still allowlist style).
_comment_hardening: Hardening posture vs. Docker's default seccomp + the earlier emulator-builder draft: (1) defaultAction is SCMP_ACT_ERRNO not SCMP_ACT_ALLOW; (2) process_vm_readv / process_vm_writev are REMOVED from allow; (3) ptrace is restricted to PTRACE_TRACEME (request==0) via arg filter — PTRACE_ATTACH/PEEK/POKE return EPERM; (4) PHASE6-NOTE: mount(2) is NO LONGER restricted to MS_BIND in this proposed L0b profile (see PHASE5-AMENDMENT group) because ReDroid init's tmpfs/proc/sysfs mounts and Magisk's `magisk --setup-sbin` tmpfs at /sbin are non-bind and seccomp CANNOT filter the fstype string (it is a userspace pointer arg); (5) init_module / finit_module / delete_module / create_module / query_module / kexec_load / kexec_file_load / reboot / iopl / ioperm / acct / quotactl / nfsservctl / vhangup / pivot_root / uselib / ustat / sysfs / setdomainname / sethostname remain DENIED by default (not listed in any allow group). PHASE6-NOTE: personality and setns, previously DENIED in the production profile, are now ALLOWED in this proposed L0b profile — re-permitting them is the documented widening required for a rooted boot. APPLIED 2026-06-01: both are now ARG-FILTERED (personality persona∈{0,0xffffffff}; setns nstype==CLONE_NEWNS) rather than unconditionally allowed, materially shrinking the personality-ASLR-off and setns-escape surfaces while still booting+rooting (empirically re-tested). process_vm_readv/writev stay removed; ptrace stays PTRACE_TRACEME-only.
_comment_compliance: refuse-privileged-compose §4 + agents/orchestrator/SPEC.md §4 compliant. NOT a substitute for cap_drop:[ALL], no-new-privileges:true, or image digest pinning. PROPOSAL — board review required before promotion. As of 2026-06-01 the audit §5 arg-filter recommendations have been APPLIED (personality + setns are now arg-filtered, not unconditional) and empirically boot+root re-tested; mount remains unfiltered (fstype non-narrowable, documented accepted tradeoff).
_proposal_provenance: Phase 6 (audit/phase6-hardened-boot-2026-05-30.md) — empirically validated full boot+root under enforcing seccomp. Amendment list derived from Phase 5 (audit/phase5-hardened-l0b-2026-05-30.md §4).

syscalls._group: PHASE5-AMENDMENT (CONDITION-2) — arch_prctl + mount only. The personality and setns syscalls that were formerly in this unconditional ALLOW have been SPLIT OUT into their own arg-filtered ALLOW groups below (APPLIED 2026-06-01 per proof/seccomp-promotion-audit/RESULT.md §5 + APPLIED.md, each empirically boot+root re-tested). Remaining two here stay UNFILTERED for the reasons stated. arch_prctl(158): Bionic linker sets the TLS base (ARCH_SET_FS) at the start of EVERY process; denied -> null-TLS segfault in linker64 (container exits 139 before init logs); seccomp cannot narrow it without breaking TLS (audit §3.1 ACCEPT-AS-IS, intra-container only). mount(165): re-permitted UNFILTERED for NON-BIND filesystems (ReDroid init tmpfs/proc/sysfs + magisk --setup-sbin tmpfs at /sbin); the production profile's MS_BIND-only arg-filter is intentionally REPLACED by this unfiltered allow because seccomp cannot narrow by fstype string (the fstype is a userspace char* arg, not a scalar seccomp can compare) — documented accepted tradeoff, NOT narrowable, left as-is. SECURITY TRADE-OFF: this still widens the profile vs production (re-permits the namespace/mount path) but the strongest restrictions are untouched: process_vm_readv/writev stay removed, ptrace stays PTRACE_TRACEME-only, init_module/kexec_*/pivot_root/swapon stay denied. Bounded by no-new-privileges:true + cap_drop:[ALL] of all NON-curated caps + not --pid=host / --network=host. NOTE (seccomp-promotion-audit 2026-06-01): CAP_SYS_ADMIN IS present in the curated HARDENED_CAP_ADD set (SPEC §4 mandates it for ReDroid boot), so setns/mount are NOT bounded by its absence — this is why setns has now been narrowed to CLONE_NEWNS below; mount cannot be narrowed (fstype is a pointer) and its residual risk is the documented accepted tradeoff.

personality-PER_LINUX-set (APPLIED 2026-06-01, boot+root re-tested in sec-pers). Allows ONLY persona==0 (PER_LINUX, the value Android/Bionic sets). BLOCKS personas with ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE(0x0040000, disables ASLR) / READ_IMPLIES_EXEC(0x0400000, defeats W^X/NX) / ADDR_COMPAT_LAYOUT bits set — closes the audit §3.2 'medium' intra-container exploit-mitigation weakening. Paired with the persona==0xffffffff query rule below. defaultAction (SCMP_ACT_ERRNO) denies every other persona value.

personality-query (APPLIED 2026-06-01). persona==0xffffffff==4294967295 is the libc 'read the current personality without changing it' query path (Bionic uses it on zygote-forked apps; denying it triggers 'F libc: error getting old personality value' -> zygote crash-loop). Allowing only the read-query plus PER_LINUX-set above preserves boot while denying ASLR-off / RIE personas.

setns-mountns-only (APPLIED 2026-06-01, boot+root re-tested in sec-setns; strace of magiskd proved it). magiskd calls setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS) to (re-)enter a target process's mount namespace for its per-process module bind-mount overlay. nstype (arg index 1) is PINNED to CLONE_NEWNS=0x00020000=131072 — this BLOCKS setns into PID (CLONE_NEWPID 0x20000000), NET (CLONE_NEWNET 0x40000000), USER (CLONE_NEWUSER 0x10000000), UTS, IPC, cgroup, AND the nstype==0 'any-type' form (the most escape-relevant case, where the kernel accepts whatever the fd points to). EMPIRICAL JUSTIFICATION: `strace -f -e trace=setns` on the live magiskd (host pid) captured 10/10 calls as setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS) with the EXPLICIT nstype — magiskd does NOT use the nstype==0 any-type form, so this filter does not break it (the audit §3.3 / RESULT.md §5 flagged risk that magiskd might use nstype=0 does NOT materialize). This materially shrinks the setns+CAP_SYS_ADMIN container-escape surface (the top residual risk per the audit) while preserving Magisk's mount-ns re-entry. defaultAction (SCMP_ACT_ERRNO) denies every other nstype.

filesystem-and-namespace-core (Android boot + Magisk overlay needs; ptrace and mount are intentionally NOT here — see arg-filtered groups below. PHASE6-NOTE: mount is now in the PHASE5-AMENDMENT group above (unfiltered), so the magisk-mount-bind-only arg-filtered group below is retained for documentation/traceability but is superseded by the broader allow.)

magisk-mount-bind-only (PHASE6-SUPERSEDED: this MS_BIND-only arg-filter on mount is now superseded by the unfiltered mount allow in the PHASE5-AMENDMENT group above. Retained here for traceability against the production profile. cpuinfo-overlay's service.sh issues `mount --bind /data/adb/modules/cpuinfo-overlay/system/etc/cpuinfo.spoofed /proc/cpuinfo` which sets MS_BIND.)

magisk-mount-unbind-and-namespace (umount/umount2/move_mount/open_tree/fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount/fspick/mount_setattr — required by Magisk's late_start_service to manage bind-mount lifecycle inside its mnt namespace; pivot_root, swapon, swapoff intentionally NOT included)

namespace-create (Android zygote + Magisk magiskhide. PHASE6-NOTE: setns is now ALLOWED in its own arg-filtered group above (setns-mountns-only) — magiskd requires it for per-process mount-namespace re-entry. The production profile's exclusion comment is preserved for traceability: 'setns intentionally NOT here — namespace re-entry would let escaped uid attach to host PID namespace'. MITIGATION IN PLACE (APPLIED 2026-06-01): the very escape this comment warns about — setns into the host PID/USER/NET namespace — is now BLOCKED at the seccomp layer, because setns is pinned to nstype==CLONE_NEWNS (mount-ns only); CLONE_NEWPID/NEWUSER/NEWNET and the nstype==0 any-type form all hit defaultAction=SCMP_ACT_ERRNO. So although CAP_SYS_ADMIN IS present in the curated HARDENED_CAP_ADD set, setns can no longer be used to enter a non-mount namespace even with that cap. clone/clone3/unshare remain unfiltered here (zygote/magiskhide need arbitrary namespace creation; these create NEW empty namespaces, not entry into existing host ones). See proof/seccomp-promotion-audit/RESULT.md + APPLIED.md.)

ptrace-TRACEME-only (request==PTRACE_TRACEME==0). PTRACE_ATTACH (16), PTRACE_PEEK* (1/2/3), PTRACE_POKE* (4/5/6) all return EPERM via defaultAction because this arg-filtered allow does not cover them. magiskhide's tracer-pid scrub on hidden processes WILL fail; L4 Shamiko (L0b-level Zygisk hide) is the intended root-hiding mechanism and does not require host-side ptrace.
perf-and-bpf (Android Profiler + RenderScript dispatch). bpf is allowed but kernel BPF JIT must be off on host.

explicit-deny-documentation (these are denied because defaultAction=SCMP_ACT_ERRNO and they appear in NO allow group above; listed here for auditor traceability only). PHASE6-NOTE: personality and setns have been MOVED OUT of this deny list into the PHASE5-AMENDMENT allow group above. Remaining forbidden syscalls: process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, init_module, finit_module, delete_module, create_module, query_module, kexec_load, kexec_file_load, reboot, iopl, ioperm, acct, quotactl, lookup_dcookie, nfsservctl, vhangup, pivot_root, swapon, swapoff, uselib, ustat, sysfs, setdomainname, sethostname.
